text: The hold that the queue-write interface obeys travels on the two events the Ownership Map gives rwb-deviation, DeviationRaised (EV-06) and DeviationCleared (EV-07), and on the case's own deviation_open flag; no REST operation is added for a queue, a hold or a placement read, and rwb-case never calls this service to place a case.
why: The S8 row of the connection matrix gives Temporal and events to P3 and no REST edge to it, the Ownership Map gives the service exactly two operations and neither reads a hold, and RWB-P3-E2036-APP refuses a placement on recovery_case.deviation_open without a synchronous call. Adding a hold read would invent an operation the map does not hold and would put a second source of truth beside the flag.

confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-case owner, before the contract is tagged
impact: The service keeps its two operations, the hold is event-driven, and a build that adds a hold read fails the absence test

text: The hold properties are additive inside major version 1 of both event envelopes: the case, the deviation, the code, the open count, the handler, the return point, the contact-stop flag and the rule version; their element names are left to the event catalogue and the service contract story and are carried as the placeholder until those publish them.
why: EV-06 and EV-07 are named by TSD S8 T5.3 and the topic by the naming rule, but no source publishes an AsyncAPI document or an element set for either envelope, and the same is true of the refusal element of the RWB-P2-E2036-CON placement contract that the hold reason must agree with.

text: The open-deviation count of a case is read inside the transaction of the raise and of the clear, as the rows of deviation of that case whose cleared_at is empty, and no counter column and no second table is added.
why: TSD S8 T3.1 gives ten fields, one handler and no counter, and FSD S8 A2.9 holds more than one open deviation on a case and resumes only when all are cleared. A stored counter would need a DB story, would drift under a concurrent clear, and would put a second authority beside the rows.

impact: The count is exact under any order of clears, the table stays as published, and no migration beyond the index is raised

text: The handler of a hold is deviation.handler_user_id and the state the case returns to is deviation.paused_state, both written at the raise and never overwritten by a placement; the clear publishes the paused state as the return point when the count reaches zero, and the case applies it under R-DEV-08 and R-DEV-18.
why: TSD S8 T3.1 names both fields and R-DEV-08 and R-DEV-18 return the case to the state it paused in; the case's route state, queue and assignment are P3's, so a second place that stored the return point would compete with the field already published.

Building the check here would duplicate it, and claiming the message as this story's deliverable would misstate where the caller is refused.

text: The one migration is a non-unique partial index on deviation (case_id) where cleared_at is null, and no unique index is used, because a case may hold more than one open deviation at a time.
why: FEAT-DVH-09 and FSD S8 A2.9 let two codes be open on one case, so a unique constraint on the open rows of a case would refuse the second raise and break the business rule the hold exists to keep. The index only serves the count read.
